entries.content: Leveraged ETFs reset daily to maintain their target multiple. This daily rebalancing creates path dependency, meaning returns over periods longer than one day depend on the sequence of daily returns, not just the cumulative index return. In volatile sideways markets, this can result in value erosion even when the underlying index is flat.

Risk capacity refers to an investor's objective financial ability to absorb losses without compromising essential goals like retirement, emergency funds, or debt obligations. It is distinct from risk tolerance, which measures psychological comfort with volatility. An investor may have high risk tolerance but low risk capacity if their financial situation cannot withstand significant portfolio losses.
